ledger.claim: CI provides green verification of the release implementation ('all eight jobs passed'; Linux '2,911 passed, 33 skipped'; hosted mutation '16 killed, zero survivors')
ledger.evidence: By the artifact's own numbers, the two recorded-digest integrity tests — test_the_artifact_is_rebuilt_from_git_with_its_recorded_digest and test_an_artifact_that_no_longer_matches_its_digest_is_refused — never execute in CI: local shows 31 skips, CI shows 33, and the text confirms they 'require a historical spec commit absent from CI's shallow checkout.' These tests cover digest rebuild and digest-mismatch refusal, yet the audit dismisses them as 'not the new containment, mutation or publication-recovery checks' while elsewhere stating the 0.13.0 changelog 'covers the integration and enforcement changes.' Furthermore, if the hosted mutation probe's 16 mutants touched that digest code, 'zero survivors' is incompatible with these tests being skipped in CI; if they did not, calling it a 'Full hosted mutation probe' overstates probe coverage.
ledger.failure_scenario: A regression in artifact-digest rebuild or digest-refusal enforcement ships in 0.13.0: every CI job is green and mutation shows zero survivors, but the only tests exercising those behaviors were skipped in all CI runs and executed solely on one developer's machine.
ledger.location: Verification evidence table; paragraph 'The local/Linux difference is two historical friend-eval provenance cases...'; header claim 'documentation head 5234def also passed all eight CI jobs'
ledger.suggested_fix: Give CI a full-history checkout (e.g., fetch-depth: 0) or vendor the historical spec commit so both tests run in CI; clarify the mutation probe's scope relative to the digest module; annotate the table that artifact-integrity tests are skipped in CI rather than letting them be subsumed under 'passed.'

ledger.claim: The named files, tests, variables, commits, and CI runs exist and match this document's descriptions

ledger.claim: The release's only remaining gate — 'Its three-round cross-examination is in progress. It must report actual participation, rounds, findings and any remaining access or model-output failures before clearance' — is a prose criterion whose trigger is paid model APIs, with no defined pass/fail test and no termination rule.
ledger.evidence: The audit itself records the trigger failing twice for reasons no deterministic test can produce: Claude hit an 'individual account spend limit', then 'Pi/GLM then timed out during critique and returned invalid judging output', each requiring ad-hoc user approval of a replacement worker. Nothing defines what mechanically distinguishes 'actual participation' from a Codex worker returning plausible hollow critique — the runtime's completeness check (tests/test_report_completeness.py) only detects *failed* friends, not vacuous ones — and no maximum number of roster replacements or fallback disposition is stated, so the approve-a-fresh-worker loop has no convergence edge any test could exercise.

Because 'clearance' has no observable output or quorum rule at the process level, the decision collapses to whoever reads the run transcripts deciding it 'looks fine' — and there is no bound after which the release process must admit the gate cannot be satisfied, so it either blocks indefinitely or is waived by the same prose flexibility that created it.
ledger.location: Artifact, 'Live cross-examination and remaining limits' section; corroborated by Makefile lines 3-5 ('Live evals ... make real model calls on your own logins ... CI runs none') and docs/superpowers/reports/2026-10-29-friend-recovery.md
